fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions on the road.
• Mark the single driveway entry clearly so responders can identify it quickly under low-light or smoke conditions.
• Clear a turnaround area near the residence large enough for a fire or rescue vehicle to reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Trim dense vegetation along the sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Cut back vegetation growing close to the main residence and detached structure so responders can move around both buildings on foot.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two without pushing through vegetation.
• Thin dense vegetation between the road and the residence so approaching responders have a clear line of sight to the structures.
• Post the property address at the driveway entrance and again near the front entry so responders can confirm they have reached the correct structure.
• Keep any perimeter gate at the driveway entrance unlocked or equipped with a Knox-style lock box so responders are not delayed by a locked entry.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back trees and shrubs that are directly touching or overhanging the structure on all sides.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open space between individual trees and between the trees and the building.
• Remove low-hanging branches from large trees near the structure up to at least 10 feet from the ground.
• Separate shrubs and ground vegetation from the base of the structure by clearing a bare or mowed buffer directly around the foundation.
• Thin scattered trees across the property to reduce the ability of fire to move from tree to tree toward the structure.
• Mow or cut down ground vegetation close to the structure, keeping it short and well away from the walls.
• Clear scattered shrubs that sit between the tree clusters and the structure to remove a direct path for fire to travel toward the building.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches, encroaching shrubs, and any vegetation that narrows the road surface.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency responders approaching from the road.
• Remove any dead plant material, dry ground cover, or accumulated leaf litter from around the structure and along the access route.
• Keep the open terrain areas adjacent to the structure free of shrub regrowth and tall
